decisions.reason: As a classic close-to-core handle line, it is still relatively cheap for a large broad-range supplier to retain, although after several years and no recent visibility its pruning risk is no longer low.
This handle family still fits the firm's established assortment and customer base, but the complexity of keeping several models means it now needs enough project demand to justify staying.

After four years the market test for a single incremental handle design should be largely resolved, and limited recent visibility makes reallocating resources more attractive than keeping the option open.
Because this is another single close-to-core design with likely overlapping substitutes in a broad portfolio, the firm would rationalize it if it has not shown clear pull by now.

Despite higher carrying and update costs, this electronic access system remains aligned with the firm's digital systems direction, so management would more likely retain or refresh it than withdraw it.
